reasoning.reconstruction: Choose a basis of W and identify V tensor W with dim(W) copies of V. If T has V-endomorphism blocks T_ab, commutation with X tensor I_W is exactly X*T_ab=T_ab*X for every X in End(V). To see that such a block is scalar without hiding a Schur hypothesis, commute it with all diagonal matrix units E_ii: its off-diagonal entries vanish. Commuting the resulting diagonal matrix with E_ij forces all diagonal entries equal. Thus T_ab=c_ab I_V and T=I_V tensor(c_ab). Conversely the mixed-factor products (X tensor I)(I tensor B)=X tensor B=(I tensor B)(X tensor I) prove the other inclusion.
reasoning.boundary: If either factor is zero dimensional, V tensor W is0 and both displayed subsets are the zero operator set; no uniqueness of the matrix(c_ab) is asserted then. For dim(V)=1 the same argument reduces to all operators on W. This full-matrix-algebra center fact in fact works over any field; algebraic closure is not needed for this particular lemma, unlike replacing End(V) by an arbitrary real irreducible group image.

reasoning.missing_dependency_reconstructed: The claim that the image algebra contains each full End(V_alpha) block and the central isotypical projections is substantive, not a consequence merely of calling the blocks irreducible. Over C for a finite group it follows from matrix-coefficient orthogonality. Choose invariant Hermitian structures on the irreducibles. For each alpha,i,j, the averaged matrix (dim(V_alpha)/|G|)*sum_g conjugate(rho_alpha(g)_ij)*rho(g) has the single alpha-block E_ij tensor I and zero other blocks. These matrix units lie in A and span the independent block algebras; summing their diagonals gives the central projections P_alpha. Conversely each rho(g) acts blockwise as rho_alpha(g) tensor I, so A is exactly their direct sum.
reasoning.commutant: An operator in A' commutes with every P_alpha, hence has no cross-isotypical blocks. On an alpha block,301 gives precisely I_V_alpha tensor End(C^n_alpha). Each such collection plainly commutes with A, giving equality. The same central projections also belong to A' (they commute with A), so elements of A'' again have no cross blocks. Applying301 with the factors reversed returns End(V_alpha) tensor I on each block and hence A''=A. This checks the otherwise implicit off-block step in the second commutant.
reasoning.boundary: Only occurring irreducible types are needed; zero multiplicities contribute no space, and the zero representation gives the empty direct sum/zero algebra. reasoning.tableau_reconstruction: For lambda_1>=lambda_2>=0, each of the first lambda_2 two-cell columns of a semistandard tableau over{1,2} is forced to have1 above2. The remaining m=lambda_1-lambda_2 cells are the top-row tail, and a weakly increasing tail is determined by the number a of its1s, with a=0,...,m. reasoning.representation_reconstruction: The source realization is det^(lambda_2) tensor Sym^m(C^2). The determinant character is one dimensional, so it does not change dimension. An occupation basis of Sym^m(C^2) has one vector for each number of1 labels from0 to m and hence dimension m+1. Equivalently Weyl's single row-pair factor gives(lambda_1-lambda_2+1)/1. Tensoring by det^lambda_2 shifts both highest-weight entries but not this difference.
